change.describe: branch `pr-37634` of keycloak-37634 against c22f76867f595f0f7c327376a66a08dca01949e8 (merge-base c22f768)
change.title: pr-37634
change.description:
Encoding context to access token IDs closes #37118
Shorter encoding of access token
change.author: mposolda

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher compares the wrong characters and the result is inverted
findings.body: The encoded id is `<st:2><tt:2><gt:2>:<uuid>`, so the grant shortcut is at indexes 4..6. The matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which spans the last character of the token type and the first character of the grant shortcut. It also returns `false` when that substring equals the expected shortcut. The substring can never equal a 2-char shortcut in a real id, so the check never rejects anything. It only verifies the `xxxxxx:<uuid>` shape, and the `expectedGrantShortcut` argument passed from `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and the others is never enforced. The matcher would also reject a correct id if the offsets were fixed without removing the negation. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, and also check that `items[0].length() == 6`, since `substring` throws on shorter input. The `describeTo` text ("Not a Token ID...") reads like the negated condition and should say what is expected.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId validates grantType instead
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` then silently produces an id ending in `:null`. Change it to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Client-credentials tokens never get GRANT_TYPE set, so they are encoded as unknown ('na')
findings.body: The PR adds the `cc` shortcut and the unit test uses `trltcc:...` as a client-credentials token. `ClientCredentialsGrantType` does not call `createTokenResponse`. It builds the token with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` (line 140) and never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on `clientSessionCtx`. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` then falls back to `UNKNOWN`, so these tokens get ids like `trrtna:<uuid>`. The same applies to the UMA path (`AuthorizationTokenService` around line 357, shortcut `pg`) and to the legacy path in `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` (around line 409). Only `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` sets the attribute. Set `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` after line 122 in `ClientCredentialsGrantType`. For the UMA and legacy token-exchange paths, either set it there or confirm that leaving them as 'na' is intended.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of a NullPointerException, not the validation it targets
findings.body: `before()` never calls `postInit`, so `factory.sessionFactory` is null. For `ofrtac:5678`, the `ac` shortcut is not in the manually populated map. `getGrantTypeByShortcut` then falls back to `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws an NPE. The test catches `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever reaching the `IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value ... for grant type")` branch. Provide a mock or stub `KeycloakSessionFactory` that returns an empty stream, and catch `IllegalArgumentException`. The `Assert.assertEquals(actual, expected)` calls throughout the file also have their arguments reversed, which makes failure messages misleading. The tests also do not cover `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (session type, lightweight and grant fallback) or the malformed-id branches (wrong length, unknown session or token type).

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant factories and null shortcuts break startup
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as a non-default method on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, so any out-of-tree grant factory stops compiling or fails with `AbstractMethodError`. If one returns null, `postInit` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` (lines 75-76) throws an NPE from `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)`, which gives a poor startup error. Consider validating non-null and exactly 2 characters in `postInit` with a clear message. Also reject a shortcut equal to `na`, which is reserved for UNKNOWN. The encoder reads exactly 2 chars (`encodedContext.length() != 6`), so a longer shortcut would produce ids the decoder rejects.

findings.title: setFormParams leaves grantType stale
findings.body: `grantType` is read from `formParams` once in the constructor, but `setFormParams` (line 105) replaces the map without refreshing it. No caller of `setFormParams` was found in the repository. If one is added later, `getGrantType()` will not reflect the new params. Either recompute it there or drop the setter. The copy constructor `Context(Context)` was also removed; a grep found no remaining callers.

contracts.action: Access token id is now `<sessionType><tokenType><grant>:<uuid>` instead of a bare UUID (TokenManager.initToken)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())`. Refresh and ID tokens still use bare UUIDs (TokenManager.java:1252, 1317).
contracts.before_after: initToken is reached only through createClientAccessToken (TokenManager.java:613), so only access-token ids change. The token id reaches events via Details.TOKEN_ID (TokenManager.java:1364, TokenRevocationEndpoint.java:119, LoginActionsService.java:586) and the `jti` claim. The encoder is resolved with session.getProvider on every token.
contracts.visible_effect: The `jti` and the `token_id` event detail change format. The unit test for the grant shortcut is vacuous because of the matcher bug in AssertEvents.
contracts.failure_mode: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException if the grant type string has no registered factory or shortcut. In that case token creation would fail with a 500. For the standard grants, the grant type comes from the validated grant_type form param or from constants, so it should resolve.

contracts.action: GRANT_TYPE attribute set on ClientSessionContext by individual grants
contracts.equivalent_path: createTokenResponse (AuthCode, Device, CIBA), ROPC (line 134), refresh (TokenManager.java:248), standard token exchange (line 237) and pre-authorized code (line 82) all set it. ClientCredentialsGrantType, UMA and the legacy token exchange do not.
contracts.before_after: Before: no grant info in the context. After: grants that skip the setter fall back to 'na' in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.
contracts.visible_effect: Client-credentials and UMA tokens carry the 'na' grant in their id, which contradicts the `cc` shortcut and the unit test fixtures.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong grant in the id; no error.

summary:
The change adds an encoder SPI that prefixes access-token ids with session type, token type and grant shortcut. I found three defects and two smaller issues.

- **Vacuous test matcher:** `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` reads `substring(3, 5)` instead of `substring(4, 6)` and negates the comparison, so it never checks the grant shortcut it is given.
- **Null check on the wrong variable:** `AccessTokenContext` validates `grantType` twice, so `rawTokenId` is never checked.
- **Client credentials encoded as unknown:** `ClientCredentialsGrantType` never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, so its tokens are encoded with the unknown grant `na` despite the `cc` shortcut. The UMA and legacy token-exchange paths have the same gap.
- **Unit test passes by accident:** `testIncorrectGrantType` passes because of a `NullPointerException` (the factory's `sessionFactory` is null), not the validation it targets.
- **Minor:** the new abstract `getShortcut()` has no validation of null or oversized shortcuts, and `Context.setFormParams` leaves `grantType` stale.

I only read the code and did not run any tests.
